title: Everyday Opposites
description: Choose familiar opposite words by reading the particular meaning supplied in each clue.
cardDescription: Choose familiar opposite words by reading the particular meaning supplied in each clue.
focus: One word can have different opposites in different contexts. Weight, brightness, direction, and position are separate comparisons even when the same short word can appear in more than one.
solvingTip: Use the context after the opposite-word hint to choose the intended meaning.
words: Opposite of heavy when comparing weight
Opposite of left when choosing a direction
Opposite of open when used as an action
Opposite of narrow when describing width
Opposite of late when describing an arrival
Opposite of full when describing a container
Opposite of noisy when describing a room
Opposite of deep when describing water
Opposite of back when describing an object's sides
Direction indicated by S on a compass card
Opposite of present when attendance is checked
Opposite of more when comparing an amount
Opposite of hard when describing a cushion
Opposite of wet when describing a cloth

answerNotes.LIGHT: Light contrasts with heavy for weight, but with dark when describing illumination.
answerNotes.RIGHT: Right is directional here rather than meaning correct or a legal entitlement.
answerNotes.CLOSE: Close is a verb here; its near meaning uses the same spelling with a different sense and pronunciation.
answerNotes.WIDE: Wide and narrow compare width rather than height or depth.
answerNotes.EARLY: Early is relative to the expected time, not one fixed hour of the day.

title: Letters You Do Not Hear
description: Identify familiar words through their meaning and a letter that is normally silent in their American pronunciation.
cardDescription: Identify familiar words through their meaning and a letter that is normally silent in their American pronunciation.
focus: English spelling sometimes preserves letters no longer heard in ordinary pronunciation. Each clue supplies the meaning as well as the silent-letter hint.
solvingTip: Solve the definition first, then check the silent letter against the crossings.
words: Blade-and-handle cutting tool whose initial k is silent
Joint between hand and forearm, with a silent initial w
Young sheep whose final b is silent
Money owed, with a silent b
Truthful, with a silent initial h
Joint between thigh and lower leg, with a silent k
Small legendary figure whose initial g is silent
Hand digit whose final b is silent
Uncertainty, with a b that is not pronounced
Land surrounded by water, with a silent s
Sixty-minute period whose initial h is silent
Sacred song word whose initial p is silent
Toothed hair tool whose final b is silent
Fortified residence word with a normally silent t

answerNotes.KNIFE: The k is retained in spelling even though ordinary pronunciation begins with the n sound.
answerNotes.WRIST: Wrist starts with a written w that is not heard in standard American pronunciation.
answerNotes.LAMB: The written b remains at the end even though the spoken word ends in an m sound.
answerNotes.DEBT: The b belongs to the spelling rather than the usual spoken sound sequence.
answerNotes.HONEST: Honest begins with a vowel sound in ordinary American English, which also explains the phrase an honest person.

title: Putting Two Small Words Together
description: Explore familiar compound words by connecting their meanings with the shorter words used to form them.
cardDescription: Explore familiar compound words by connecting their meanings with the shorter words used to form them.
focus: A compound combines smaller words into an established expression. Some clues ask for the whole compound, while others ask for one component named in the clue.
solvingTip: Check whether the definition asks for the finished word or only its first or second part.
words: Brewing vessel whose name joins a leaf drink and a cooking container
Evening event named by joining our star and a word for going down
Tiny biting insect: bed plus bug
Small writing-fluid container named from fluid and a hollow
Couch-like bed whose name begins with the opposite of night
Pronoun for any person, formed as a single compound word
Visitor signal whose name joins an entrance panel and a ringing device
First component of the word sunlight
Final component of the word mailbox
First component of the word daytime
Final component of the word doorbell
Final component of the word flowerbed
First component of the word teacup
Final component of the word flowerpot
First component of the word inkpot

answerNotes.TEAPOT: Teapot combines tea and pot into one established word naming a particular vessel.
answerNotes.SUNSET: Sunset is written as one word; the combined meaning is more specific than either part alone.
answerNotes.BEDBUG: Bedbug is a compound name, not a scientific claim that every insect found near a bed belongs to that group.
answerNotes.COWBOY: Cowboy is an established occupation word; its components do not mean that every worker is a child.
answerNotes.INKWELL: Inkwell combines ink and well, using well for a holding hollow rather than only a water source.

title: What Familiar Abbreviations Mean
description: Expand common American abbreviations for titles, addresses, and everyday measurements.
cardDescription: Expand common American abbreviations for titles, addresses, and everyday measurements.
focus: The clue supplies a shortened form and asks for its ordinary expanded word. Context matters because the same abbreviation can mean something different in a specialized field.
solvingTip: Look at the category: person’s title, street address, or measurement.
words: Title commonly abbreviated Dr. before a person's name
Courtesy title usually written as Mr.
Unit whose ordinary abbreviation is oz.
Address word commonly abbreviated St. in a road name
Military-post word commonly abbreviated Ft. in place names
Title commonly abbreviated St. before a person's name

answerNotes.DOCTOR: Doctor is the expanded title; it can refer to different professional or academic qualifications.
answerNotes.MISTER: Mister is the spoken expansion of Mr.; the shortened written form is more common before a surname.
answerNotes.JUNIOR: Junior distinguishes names within a naming convention, not necessarily the youngest person in an entire family.
answerNotes.AVENUE: Avenue is an address term; the abbreviation does not require one fixed road width or layout.
answerNotes.OUNCE: Ounce can measure weight; fluid ounce is a separate volume unit with an additional qualifier.

title: Words on American Road Signs
description: Recognize short road-sign words through direct definitions of directions, conditions, and traffic arrangements.
cardDescription: Recognize short road-sign words through direct definitions of directions, conditions, and traffic arrangements.
focus: A sign’s word identifies its general message. This puzzle is a vocabulary scene, with different terms for a route change, joining traffic, and a single travel direction.
solvingTip: Use the kind of message: warning, payment, direction, or road feature.
words: Road-sign instruction to give priority to other traffic when required
Alternate route around a closed or obstructed road
To join another stream of traffic
Charge paid for using a particular road or crossing
Single-direction traffic arrangement, with spaces omitted
Instruction requiring a complete halt at a road sign
Word advising reduced speed in a marked area
Marked route leading off a highway
One marked strip of roadway for a line of vehicles
Word identifying an area associated with pupils and a nearby campus
Bend in the road shown by a warning sign
Raised uneven part of a road surface
Short low section of a road surface
Connecting sloped roadway leading to or from a highway

answerNotes.YIELD: Yield concerns right of way; it is different from an unconditional instruction to stop in every situation.
answerNotes.DETOUR: A detour changes the route temporarily rather than necessarily changing the destination.
answerNotes.MERGE: Merge describes joining flows, distinct from simply crossing a road.
answerNotes.TOLL: A toll is a use charge rather than a speed or distance measurement.
answerNotes.ONEWAY: One way describes the permitted travel direction; the words are continuous in the grid.
